Tradovate API
Which Tradovate API access do you need?​

This guide documents CrossTrade's API for linked Tradovate accounts. It does not describe signing up for a separate native Tradovate developer account. CrossTrade API access requires Pro, a CrossTrade Bearer token and a linked Tradovate identity. See current CrossTrade pricing for the plan; broker, market-data and any direct Tradovate API arrangements are separate.

Begin with GET /v1/api/tv/status and GET /v1/api/tv/accounts. Confirm the linked environment and returned account names before trying an order request. These reads do not place a trade. NinjaTrader does not have to be installed or running for this cloud route.

If your goal is to send TradingView alerts rather than build a REST client, use Tradovate webhook automation and its setup guide. Webhook messages use a different authentication credential and interface from the REST examples here.

The /v1/api/tv surface exposes your linked Tradovate accounts through CrossTrade. It is separate from the NinjaTrader /v1/api surface:

PLATFORM	ROUTE PREFIX	RUNTIME	WEBSOCKET
Tradovate	/v1/api/tv	Server-side against your linked Tradovate identity. NT8 can be closed.	Supported: events, P&L, and RPC with origin: "tradovate". No market data.
NinjaTrader 8	/v1/api	Through the CrossTrade NT8 Add-On in a running NT8 desktop instance.	Supported.
HOW THE TRADOVATE DOCS ARE ORGANIZED

Most Tradovate endpoints mirror an existing NinjaTrader endpoint. Those shared endpoints are documented on their existing reference pages, where a Tradovate tab sits beside the NT8 tab (for example POST Place Order, GET All Orders, and POST Close Position).

The pages in this Tradovate section are the endpoints unique to Tradovate, with no NT8 equivalent: link status, cash balances, margin snapshots, contract lookup and suggestions, current-session fills, durable fill history, and the exchange list.

The two tables below index the whole surface, shared and Tradovate-only, in one place.

Tradovate reads return account state such as positions, orders, fills, and balances. Order and fill lists mirror Tradovate's own API, which only tracks the current trading session: those lists reset at the daily session close (around 5:00 PM ET) and stay empty until the next open, including all weekend. For a durable record of executions, use GET Fill History, which is served from CrossTrade's continuous capture rather than Tradovate's session data. Mutations such as place, cancel, change, close, flatten, and reverse run server-side through the same validation and controls as a Tradovate webhook signal: field validation, Account Manager kill or closing-only checks, position gates, and Trade Copier fan-out all apply. Because these are direct REST calls rather than inbound webhook alerts, the webhook-only layers do not apply: there is no webhook secret or channel to validate, no Alert History entry, no news lockout, no webhook rate bucket, and no per-account/instrument webhook lock.

GENERALLY AVAILABLE

Tradovate-native REST routing, the API Playground, MCP Tv_* tools, and the CrossTrade-exclusive ATM layer (target-fill breakeven, profit-triggered trail activation, and durable trigger replay) are generally available.

The endpoints that exist only on the Tradovate surface.

Native Tradovate vs. CrossTrade-exclusive​
CAPABILITY	OWNER
Market/limit/stop/MIT/trailing orders, OSO/OCO brackets, multibracket targets and stops, continuous ATM trailing	Tradovate native
Reusable named Tradovate ATM configurations	CrossTrade webhook configuration; REST and MCP use inline atm* fields
Profit-triggered trail activation and durable restart replay	CrossTrade-exclusive for the tier's whole life: CrossTrade ratchets the ordinary stop, never converting it to a native Tradovate trailing stop
Target-fill breakeven	CrossTrade-exclusive; Tradovate AutoBracket has no breakeven field

No fresh price means fail closed; for a pending managed trail, the native fixed stop remains active.

Prerequisites​
Link a Tradovate account. Connect at least one Tradovate identity under My Account, Brokers tab. Requests for an unlinked user return 403 tradovate_not_linked.
API access on your plan. The same plan gate as /v1/api applies (Pro). Requests without it return 401 api_requires_pro. The webhook route (destination=tradovate;) is available on every plan.
A bearer token. Use the same token as the rest of the CrossTrade API. See Authentication.
Base URL and auth​

All paths are under https://app.crosstrade.io. Every request carries a bearer token:

NAME	VALUE
Content-Type	application/json
Authorization	Bearer <token>

The {account} path segment is the Tradovate account name (for example DEMO12345678), matched case-insensitively.

Response envelope​

Most reads return {"success": true, "data": ...}. The accounts snapshot is the exception: it returns its snapshot object directly, including success, accounts, asOf, and counts. Mutations return the dispatcher envelope:

{

  "success": true,

  "destination": "tradovate",

  "api": "place_order",

  "account": "DEMO12345678",

  "instrument": "MES1!",

  "response": { "orderId": 123456789 },

  "durationMs": 214

}


A bracketed placement (takeProfit and/or stopLoss) is one Tradovate placeOSO call, and response carries all three native ids: orderId is the entry, oso1Id and oso2Id are the children in the order they were sent (take-profit, then stop-loss; a single-leg bracket only has oso1Id), and osoChildIds repeats the child ids as an array. An inline ATM placement returns orderStrategyId instead of orderId, without a resolved child-order map. Public REST and MCP do not expose a strategy-child lookup.

{

  "success": true,

  "destination": "tradovate",

  "api": "place_with_brackets",

  "account": "DEMO12345678",

  "instrument": "MES1!",

  "response": { "orderId": 123456789, "oso1Id": 123456790, "oso2Id": 123456791, "osoChildIds": [123456790, 123456791] },

  "durationMs": 231

}


An id in the response means Tradovate accepted the order. It does not mean the order is resting or filled: see Late rejections below.

Validation and account-lock failures use {"success": false, "error": "<message>"}. Failures after dispatch begins may also include dispatcher context such as destination, api, account, instrument, and durationMs. These failures use a 400 status unless an authentication or rate-limit status below applies.

Read endpoints​

Shared endpoints link to their NinjaTrader twin page, which carries a Tradovate section. Tradovate-only endpoints link to their own pages.

METHOD	PATH	DESCRIPTION
GET	/v1/api/tv/status	Token and connection status for your Tradovate identities.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts	List your linked Tradovate accounts.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/snapshot	Live per-account P&L, positions, and working orders in one call.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}	One account plus a cash-balance snapshot.
GET	/v1/api/tv/positions	Open positions across all linked accounts.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions	Open positions on one account.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/position?instrument=	Single net position for one account and instrument. netPos is signed; 0 means flat. Raw Tradovate row: can lag a fill by tens of seconds. Use the account's /positions read for a live net.
GET	/v1/api/tv/orders	Every current-session order across all linked accounts.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders	Working orders on one account.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}	One order by Tradovate order id.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/status	Slim order status: id, status, action, contract, timestamp.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/lifecycle	Order audit trail: order, version, commands, and command reports (with reject reasons).
GET	/v1/api/tv/fills	Current-session fills across linked accounts.
GET	/v1/api/tv/fills/history	Durable fill history captured by the CrossTrade journal; survives the daily session reset.
GET	/v1/api/tv/fills/order/{orderId}	Current-session fills for one Tradovate order id.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/fills	Current-session fills for one account's identity.
GET	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/watermarks	P&L high-water marks tracked by the Account Manager monitor engine.
GET	/v1/api/tv/cashbalances	Cash-balance snapshots.
GET	/v1/api/tv/marginsnapshots	Margin snapshots.
GET	/v1/api/tv/contracts/find?name=	Resolve a contract by exact symbol.
GET	/v1/api/tv/contracts/suggest?text=	Contract search suggestions; resolves the active front month.
GET	/v1/api/tv/exchanges	Exchange reference list.
Trading endpoints​
METHOD	PATH	DESCRIPTION
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/place	Place an order, including native OSO/OCO and multibracket orders plus CrossTrade-exclusive managed ATM enhancements.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/cancel	Cancel one order.
PUT	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/change	Change one order. Supports partial changes with required live fields restored before submission. POST is still accepted for backward compatibility.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/replace	Durably cancel and replace one order on the same account and contract.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/cancel	Cancel working orders on the account.
POST	/v1/api/tv/orders/cancelall	Cancel all working orders.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/cancel_and_bracket	Cancel all working orders on the account/instrument, then protect the current position with a bracket. action is the protected position side. The hyphen form cancel-and-bracket is also accepted.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/flatplace	Flatten the position and clear same-contract working orders, confirm settlement, then place a new order.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions/close	Close a position, full or partial by qty or percent.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions/flatten	Flatten one account.
POST	/v1/api/tv/positions/flatten	Flatten every linked account.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions/reverse	Reverse the position.
POST	/v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions/reverseposition	Reverse the position (position-scoped variant).
MCP tools​

Elite subscribers can call this same surface through the hosted MCP server as Tv_* tools. Reads map to the endpoints above (for example Tv_ListAccounts, Tv_AccountSnapshot, Tv_GetPosition), and trades (for example Tv_PlaceOrder, Tv_ClosePosition, Tv_FlattenEverything) run through the same validation and controls, so Account Manager locks and Trade Copier fan-out apply there too. See Tradovate MCP tools.

Request fields​

Mutation bodies use camelCase JSON keys, matching the NinjaTrader REST surface. The command and account come from the path, so a body only needs the trade fields. Common fields:

FIELD	EXAMPLE	NOTES
instrument	MES1!	Symbol. Continuous (MES1!), NT8 expiry (MES 12-26), or Tradovate contract (MESZ6) forms are accepted.
action	buy / sell	Order side.
qty	1	Quantity. quantity is also accepted.
orderType	market / limit / stop	Required for entry endpoints. Stop-limit, MIT, and trailing variants are also supported.
limitPrice	5000.25	Required for limit orders.
stopPrice	4995.00	Required for stop orders.
takeProfit	5020.00	Optional absolute bracket target. REST does not run webhook relative-price preprocessing. Sent as a GTC limit leg of a native OSO; the price is fixed at submission and never recalculated from the fill.
stopLoss	4990.00	Optional absolute bracket stop. REST does not run webhook relative-price preprocessing. Sent as a GTC stop leg of the same OSO; with takeProfit the two legs are OCO-linked by Tradovate.
orderId	entry-2026-09-06-001	Optional tracking id you choose (up to 64 characters). For ordinary orders, remembered for seven days so later cancel, change, and replace calls can reference it, and forwarded as clOrdId unless you supply that separately. Inline ATM placement stores it as a strategy reference after acceptance, not as a broker client-order id; without notes or clOrdId, it becomes the entry order's text.
clOrdId	entry-2026-09-06-001	Optional client order id sent to Tradovate for ordinary placement (up to 64 characters). Inline ATM placement has no client order id; without notes, the value becomes the entry order's text instead. Tradovate does not reject a repeated clOrdId; it is a label for reconciliation, not an idempotency key.
atmTargets	20,40	Tradovate native: per-tier target distances, in ticks by default or points with pt.
atmStops	15	Tradovate native: one stop distance for all tiers or one per tier.
atmQtys	1,1	Tradovate native: contracts per tier; must sum to qty.
atmTrail	false,true	Tradovate native without a trigger: continuously trail selected tiers from entry.
atmTrailTrigger	,30	CrossTrade-exclusive: profit distance that activates selected trailing tiers. Pair with atmTrailOffset. Day entries only.
atmTrailOffset	,10	CrossTrade-managed activation, native handoff: native trail distance after confirmed conversion.
atmBreakeven	1	CrossTrade-exclusive: target tier whose fill moves surviving stops to breakeven. Day entries only.
atmBreakevenOffset	2	CrossTrade-exclusive: ticks or points past entry for the managed breakeven stop.
percent	0.5	For positions/close, close half. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1.
outOfSync	wait	With Strategy Sync, wait withholds this request's entry and returns. It never queues the order for later placement.

See Destinations for Tradovate-specific requirements and guarantees. Shared field names do not imply identical broker sequencing.

Mutation safety​
CANCELREPLACE is owner-fenced and durable. Concurrent operations on the same order are serialized, and staged recovery state is persisted before each broker mutation. The original order must belong to the {account} in the path, and the replacement instrument must resolve to the same exact contract. CrossTrade confirms the leader cancellation and every mapped signal-copier follower cancellation before replacement fan-out. If a cancel or placement outcome is ambiguous, CrossTrade does not resend it and returns reconciliation_required; reconcile the broker orders before starting a different replacement.
Partial CHANGE requests restore broker-required fields. When omitted, CrossTrade reads and restores quantity, order type, the limit and/or stop price required by the final order type, and the trailing offset required by trailing orders. Copied followers restore those fields from each follower's own live order version before their modify request.
CANCELANDBRACKET protects an existing side. action=buy means the live position being protected is long; action=sell means it is short. It is not the side of the exit orders. A flat position or side mismatch is rejected before cancellation.
FLATPLACE fails closed on settlement. The entry is sent only after the same account and contract report a flat position and no nonterminal working orders. A timeout returns an error without placing the entry; mapped followers run their own settlement barrier.
Example: place a market order​

POST /v1/api/tv/accounts/DEMO12345678/orders/place

TOKEN="my-secret-token"



curl -X POST "https://app.crosstrade.io/v1/api/tv/accounts/DEMO12345678/orders/place" \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

  -d '{"instrument": "MES1!", "action": "buy", "qty": 1, "orderType": "market"}'


A limit order with a bracket looks like this:

curl -X POST "https://app.crosstrade.io/v1/api/tv/accounts/DEMO12345678/orders/place" \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

  -d '{"instrument": "MES1!", "action": "buy", "qty": 2, "orderType": "limit", "limitPrice": 5000.25, "takeProfit": 5020.00, "stopLoss": 4990.00}'


A two-tier native multibracket with a CrossTrade-exclusive triggered runner:

curl -X POST "https://app.crosstrade.io/v1/api/tv/accounts/DEMO12345678/orders/place" \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

  -d '{"instrument":"MES1!","action":"buy","qty":2,"orderType":"market","tif":"day","atmTargets":"20,40","atmStops":"15","atmQtys":"1,1","atmTrail":"false,true","atmTrailTrigger":"30","atmTrailOffset":"10"}'


Tradovate hosts the entry, targets, fixed stops, and OCO structure. CrossTrade tracks the trade's best price and arms the runner only after the 30-tick trigger. From then on it keeps tightening the runner's ordinary stop to stay 10 ticks behind the best price, confirming each move with the broker; the stop is never converted to a native Tradovate trailing stop.

Locks and trade copier​

Because mutations flow through the same validation and controls as a webhook signal, two behaviors are shared:

Account locks apply. If the Tradovate Account Manager (or the account's own Block Signals switch) has locked the account, a blocked request returns {"success": false, "error": "Signal blocked, kill switch engaged ..."}. Cancels, closes, and flattens still go through on a locked account. Order changes do not, because a change can loosen a stop as easily as tighten it. A closing-only lock rejects opening orders unless they carry flatten-first semantics.
Copiers fan out. If a signal-mode Trade Copier is configured on the account as a leader, an order placed here mirrors to its followers, exactly as a webhook would.

Master Controls are not account locks. The master Kill Switch, the global Closing Only switch, and the global Trading Window apply to webhook alerts only and do not block these API requests.

Errors​
STATUS	ERROR	MEANING
400	tradovate_rejected	Tradovate rejected the request (invalid price, insufficient funds, and similar). detail carries the broker's reason.
401	invalid_bearer	Missing or invalid token.
401	inactive_subscription	Subscription is not active.
401	api_requires_pro	Your plan does not include API access.
403	tradovate_not_linked	No linked Tradovate identity on your account.
403	tradovate_session_expired	Your Tradovate session expired. Reconnect the account under My Account, Brokers. Retrying does not help: requests for that login keep failing until it is reconnected.
403	endpoint_not_available	Path is not part of the current /v1/api/tv surface.
409	account_ambiguous	The account name exists on more than one linked identity. Rename one so every linked account name is unique.
429	rate_limited	CrossTrade API request budget exceeded (180 requests/min per user). Includes a Retry-After header and retryAfter body field.
429	broker_rate_limited	Tradovate's own rate-limit penalty is active on your linked identity: a penalty ticket (p-ticket, p-time, p-message) on an endpoint, or Tradovate's user-level 429. When CrossTrade has already recorded that penalty window for the login it refuses the request without sending it, since sending would extend the penalty, and Retry-After carries the remaining time. CrossTrade does not pace the requests you make on this surface. Not the CrossTrade API's inbound limit. Includes Retry-After and retryAfter. See Rate limits on Tradovate.
429	snapshot_refresh_pending	Another account balance refresh is still in progress. Includes Retry-After: 1 and retryAfter: 1; retry after that delay. This is contention, not a rate-limit penalty or broker outage.
429	egress_limited	Response egress budget exceeded.
500	internal_error	Unexpected server error. Reads are safe to retry once. For a mutation, reconcile first (below); contact support if it persists.
502	tradovate_unavailable	Tradovate did not respond within 30 seconds or returned a server error. Reads are safe to retry shortly. A mutation that gets this may still have reached Tradovate: CrossTrade never resends it, and neither should you until you have reconciled (below).
503	temporarily_disabled	The Tradovate API is paused by a kill switch.

Distinguish 429 responses by error: rate_limited is CrossTrade's inbound request budget (see Rate Limiting), broker_rate_limited is the broker-side limit, and snapshot_refresh_pending means another balance refresh is still in progress. Honor the returned Retry-After header rather than treating these as the same condition. Mutations blocked by a broker penalty return broker_rate_limited along with the usual dispatcher context fields (destination, api, account, instrument, durationMs).

Reconciling an ambiguous placement​

The client-order-id procedure below applies to ordinary placements, including simple OSO brackets, not inline ATM strategies. ATM placement does not submit clOrdId as a client order id (without notes, it becomes the entry order's text, visible in Tradovate), and an orderStrategyId cannot be used with the order read endpoints. A missing local strategy reference does not prove an ambiguous ATM request failed; verify broker state before resubmitting.

A placement whose outcome you did not learn (a tradovate_unavailable or internal_error reply, or your own HTTP client timing out before CrossTrade answered) may or may not exist at the broker. Neither CrossTrade nor Tradovate deduplicates a plain placement: Tradovate accepts a repeated clOrdId, and CrossTrade's idempotency keys cover only its own composite commands (cancelreplace, copier fan-out). Resending blind can double your exposure. Instead:

Put your own intent id on every placement (orderId or clOrdId, above).
After an ambiguous reply, read GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders (working orders) and GET /v1/api/tv/orders (every order of the session), and narrow to the contract and side.
For each candidate, GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/orders/{id}/lifecycle: the New entry in commands carries the clOrdId you sent. A match is your order; its order.ordStatus and the reports tell you what became of it.
Read GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions (fill-reconciled) to learn whether anything filled meanwhile.
Place again only when no order carries your id.
Late rejections​

Tradovate can accept a placement (HTTP 2xx with an id) and reject it at its risk layer about a second later; a price outside the product's exchange price bands (InvalidPrice) is the common case. CrossTrade re-reads every accepted order a few seconds after placement. If it was rejected, an order_rejected alert goes out through your configured alert channels with Tradovate's reason, and a webhook placement's Alert History row gains a warning. REST and MCP placements have no Alert History row, so a REST integration that needs the outcome synchronously should read GET .../orders/{id}/status (or the lifecycle) itself a few seconds after placing.

Freshness​

These REST endpoints are request/response reads; the separate WebSocket event feed is described below. Plan for the following:

Balances are cached briefly. GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account} serves Tradovate's cash-balance snapshot cached for about four seconds per account; GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/snapshot is served from your login's live account stream when one is running (source: "ws", asOf the stream's last publish time, at most 15 seconds old) and otherwise read from Tradovate and cached for three seconds (source: "rest", asOf the retrieval time, so an identical asOf on two calls means you received the cached payload). GET /v1/api/tv/cashbalances returns Tradovate's rows with Tradovate's own timestamp of the last change.
Your reads go straight to Tradovate. CrossTrade paces only the traffic it generates for your login (copier, Account Manager, sync). Requests you make on this surface are sent as they arrive and count toward Tradovate's per-login limits; a penalty they draw comes back as broker_rate_limited with the remaining time.
Positions: use the fill-reconciled read. GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/positions derives the live net from the fill stream. GET /v1/api/tv/positions and the singular GET /v1/api/tv/accounts/{account}/position return Tradovate's raw position rows, which can report the pre-fill state for tens of seconds after a fill.
Orders and fills are live but session-scoped. GET .../orders and GET .../fills read Tradovate directly; row timestamps are Tradovate server timestamps. Both lists reset at the daily close. GET /v1/api/tv/fills/history is CrossTrade's durable capture of the same fills, written periodically rather than in real time.
No quotes. There is no bid, ask, or last-trade endpoint on /v1/api/tv and no Tv_* quote tool. The NinjaTrader quote endpoint requires the Add-On. Bring your own market data for dispatch decisions.
Event feed over the WebSocket. Order, fill, and position events plus account P&L stream on /ws/stream with origin: "tradovate"; no polling budget is consumed by received frames. Market data is not streamed.
Limitations​
Orders placed manually in the Tradovate app, or from any other platform, never pass through CrossTrade, so Account Manager kill and closing-only locks cannot intercept them. The read endpoints above still return them (they are pass-throughs of Tradovate's own order, position, and fill lists), and Account Manager rules evaluate the whole account's broker state, so a rule can still flatten after the fact.
Enforcement and live data run server-side, so flatten and lock latency is measured in seconds, not milliseconds.
Tradovate's API does not expose a prop firm's trailing drawdown figure, and CrossTrade has no endpoint that returns one. The Account Manager enforces the daily loss and trailing drawdown rules you configure, against its own high-water marks (GET .../watermarks).
The REST surface requires the Pro plan. The webhook destination=tradovate route is available on every plan.

Account names in this doc are placeholders (DEMO12345678); use your own.

Profit-triggered trail activation and durable restart replay	CrossTrade-exclusive for the tier's whole life: CrossTrade ratchets the ordinary stop, never converting it to a native Tradovate trailing stop
Target-fill breakeven	CrossTrade-exclusive; Tradovate AutoBracket has no breakeven field

NAME	VALUE
Content-Type	application/json
Authorization	Bearer <token>

FIELD	EXAMPLE	NOTES
instrument	MES1!	Symbol. Continuous (MES1!), NT8 expiry (MES 12-26), or Tradovate contract (MESZ6) forms are accepted.
action	buy / sell	Order side.
qty	1	Quantity. quantity is also accepted.
orderType	market / limit / stop	Required for entry endpoints. Stop-limit, MIT, and trailing variants are also supported.
limitPrice	5000.25	Required for limit orders.
stopPrice	4995.00	Required for stop orders.
takeProfit	5020.00	Optional absolute bracket target. REST does not run webhook relative-price preprocessing. Sent as a GTC limit leg of a native OSO; the price is fixed at submission and never recalculated from the fill.
stopLoss	4990.00	Optional absolute bracket stop. REST does not run webhook relative-price preprocessing. Sent as a GTC stop leg of the same OSO; with takeProfit the two legs are OCO-linked by Tradovate.
orderId	entry-2026-09-06-001	Optional tracking id you choose (up to 64 characters). For ordinary orders, remembered for seven days so later cancel, change, and replace calls can reference it, and forwarded as clOrdId unless you supply that separately. Inline ATM placement stores it as a strategy reference after acceptance, not as a broker client-order id; without notes or clOrdId, it becomes the entry order's text.
clOrdId	entry-2026-09-06-001	Optional client order id sent to Tradovate for ordinary placement (up to 64 characters). Inline ATM placement has no client order id; without notes, the value becomes the entry order's text instead. Tradovate does not reject a repeated clOrdId; it is a label for reconciliation, not an idempotency key.
atmTargets	20,40	Tradovate native: per-tier target distances, in ticks by default or points with pt.
atmStops	15	Tradovate native: one stop distance for all tiers or one per tier.
atmQtys	1,1	Tradovate native: contracts per tier; must sum to qty.
atmTrail	false,true	Tradovate native without a trigger: continuously trail selected tiers from entry.
atmTrailTrigger	,30	CrossTrade-exclusive: profit distance that activates selected trailing tiers. Pair with atmTrailOffset. Day entries only.
atmTrailOffset	,10	CrossTrade-managed activation, native handoff: native trail distance after confirmed conversion.
atmBreakeven	1	CrossTrade-exclusive: target tier whose fill moves surviving stops to breakeven. Day entries only.
atmBreakevenOffset	2	CrossTrade-exclusive: ticks or points past entry for the managed breakeven stop.
percent	0.5	For positions/close, close half. Must be greater than 0 and at most 1.
outOfSync	wait	With Strategy Sync, wait withholds this request's entry and returns. It never queues the order for later placement.

STATUS	ERROR	MEANING
400	tradovate_rejected	Tradovate rejected the request (invalid price, insufficient funds, and similar). detail carries the broker's reason.
401	invalid_bearer	Missing or invalid token.
401	inactive_subscription	Subscription is not active.
401	api_requires_pro	Your plan does not include API access.
403	tradovate_not_linked	No linked Tradovate identity on your account.
403	tradovate_session_expired	Your Tradovate session expired. Reconnect the account under My Account, Brokers. Retrying does not help: requests for that login keep failing until it is reconnected.
403	endpoint_not_available	Path is not part of the current /v1/api/tv surface.
409	account_ambiguous	The account name exists on more than one linked identity. Rename one so every linked account name is unique.
429	rate_limited	CrossTrade API request budget exceeded (180 requests/min per user). Includes a Retry-After header and retryAfter body field.
429	broker_rate_limited	Tradovate's own rate-limit penalty is active on your linked identity: a penalty ticket (p-ticket, p-time, p-message) on an endpoint, or Tradovate's user-level 429. When CrossTrade has already recorded that penalty window for the login it refuses the request without sending it, since sending would extend the penalty, and Retry-After carries the remaining time. CrossTrade does not pace the requests you make on this surface. Not the CrossTrade API's inbound limit. Includes Retry-After and retryAfter. See Rate limits on Tradovate.
429	snapshot_refresh_pending	Another account balance refresh is still in progress. Includes Retry-After: 1 and retryAfter: 1; retry after that delay. This is contention, not a rate-limit penalty or broker outage.
429	egress_limited	Response egress budget exceeded.
500	internal_error	Unexpected server error. Reads are safe to retry once. For a mutation, reconcile first (below); contact support if it persists.
502	tradovate_unavailable	Tradovate did not respond within 30 seconds or returned a server error. Reads are safe to retry shortly. A mutation that gets this may still have reached Tradovate: CrossTrade never resends it, and neither should you until you have reconciled (below).
503	temporarily_disabled	The Tradovate API is paused by a kill switch.
